findings.what: Every prediction depends on code matches: P1 needs the placeholder to match nothing, and P2-P5 need the later upgrades to match. For 11 of the 12 implementations, that code still has no anchor in the repository; only the last is anchored, by I23. The only check is a process step: the build's review reads the code again 'from a second provider'. The prereg says neither what follows if that read disagrees with a committed code file or cannot be done, nor what counts as a second provider.
findings.why: If the consequence is not fixed before the outcome, a mismatch can be explained away after the fact. The check has no teeth unless its result is defined in advance.
findings.fix: State in the prompt and in H7 what happens on a disagreement or failed read. Record both providers' sha256s in the build review and report the disagreement under Surprises. Every prediction whose verdict depends on that implementation's match is then recorded as UNKNOWN, not scored. Also require the second provider to be an RPC host other than the sidecar's.

findings.what: Line 97 says the scripts and sources read were all at the head commit and 'None was read at an older tag'. Line 107 then lists 'Rollup.sol's initializer signatures at v0.4.1, v0.4.10 and the head'.
findings.why: The F21 disclosure contradicts itself about what was read.
findings.fix: Reword line 97, for example: 'Scripts were read at the head commit only; Rollup.sol's initializer signatures also at v0.4.1 and v0.4.10.'

findings.where: tests_m3/test_history.py:14-23 (docstring: 'The key's thresholds hold their sha256s, checked by TestInstrument', listing the sidecar, the basis and tests_m3/_i63.py) and :188-203 (test_the_key_pins_the_instruments); spec/M3/predictions.json, I63 thresholds
findings.what: The thresholds pin the sidecar, the basis and the contract docstring, but tests_m3/_i63.py has only a path ('instrument'), and the pin test does not hash it. In practice the instrument is protected by holon audit prereg, which fingerprints the functions and module-level statements of helper modules. That is a different mechanism from the one the contract states.
findings.why: The contract misstates how its own instrument is fixed, and the key, which is immutable after the push, is the only place a real pin could go.
findings.fix: Before the push, either (a) add instrument_sha256 f3640dcad40aac24f55aecaf2fbff7c20c83423e5431b29a564baedf9bbee5de to the thresholds and assert it in test_the_key_pins_the_instruments, or (b) reword the docstring to say the audit fingerprints the instrument. If the docstring changes, recompute contract_docstring_sha256.

findings.what: P4's guard ('at least two upgrades are matched') counts the last upgrade. R1 already records its match, to the head's version, which is the highest version and so can never be a downgrade. The guard therefore needs only one match that was not known in advance.
findings.why: The no-downgrade check can rest on a single blind data point.
findings.fix: Optionally count matched upgrades before the last (at least 2), as P2 and P5 already exclude the last upgrade.

findings.what: The disclosed cutover log with topic 0 0xaf9f8e4eb71b2fdd... is keccak256('SubmitterContractUpdated(address,address,uint256)'). Only initialize4 emits it (Rollup.sol:217 at v0.6.3 and at the head). The receipt also held exactly one proxy Initialized log, so before the prereg it followed that initialize4 ran in the cutover transaction and initialize3 did not. That rules out one way P5's 'versions 1, 2 and 3 logged before the last upgrade' could fail: initialize3 running in the cutover. It does not decide P5.
findings.why: A reader should be able to see this inference without recomputing the topic.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the disclosure that names the event and draws this inference.

findings.where: prompts/I63_history.md:30 ('the receipt hash I59 committed weeks ago')
findings.what: I59's index was committed on 2026-10-13 (46ba230a), eight days before this prereg.
findings.why: This is a small overstatement. The point it supports still holds: the hashes were fetched by another iteration, before and independently of this build.

findings.what: decode() reads lg['topics'][0] for every log the proxy emitted. A topic-less (anonymous, LOG0) proxy log would raise IndexError rather than being skipped or refused with InstrumentError. No Rollup version, no proxy and no EmptyContract emits an anonymous event (git grep at four refs), so there is no effect on this target.
findings.why: This matters only for the generic extractor on other targets.
findings.fix: Optionally skip logs without topics, in the instrument before the push and in holon's implementation.
